rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi speculates that some ark wood remained as a sign; relics need not last, since the Prophet’s minbar wood burned or was eaten by termites and became blessed objects.
rows.anchor: لعل بقاء بعض خشبها لكونها آية وعبرة وإلا فهو ليس بأفضل من أخشاب منبر نبينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares the ark with Abraham’s stone station, whose trace wore away through repeated hand rubbing; what is now called the station is the place where it stood.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أن مقام ابراهيم عليه السلام مع كونه حجرا صلدا لم يبق أثره بكثرة مسح الأيدي

rows.speaker: عين المعاني
rows.claim: Ayn al-Maʿani takes “We left it” as the general drowning, with the object or sign mentioned before its explanatory referent.
rows.anchor: وفي عين المعاني ولقد تركناها أي الغرق العام وهو إضمار الآية قبل الذكر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the ship species itself became a sign because people had not known ships before the Flood and began making them afterward.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : يعني جنس السفينة صارت عبرة لأن الناس لم يعرفوا قبل ذلك سفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi objects that people could not have known the ship if only the encircling ocean existed before the Flood; he explains present seas through post-Flood waters and distinguishes the ocean, created from earth’s foam.
rows.anchor: كيف يعرفونها ولم يكن في الدنيا قبل الطوفان إلا البحر المحيط وذلك أن الله تعالى أمر الأرض بعد الطوفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was a carpenter, and Gabriel taught him how to build the ark.
rows.anchor: وكان نوح عليه السلام نجارا فجاء جبريل وعلمه صنعة السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mindful person should take the sign as a lesson, fear God, and abandon sin.
rows.anchor: أي معتبر بتلك الآية الحقيقة بالاعتبار فيخاف من الله ويترك المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form derives from mudhtakir on the iftiʿāl pattern; its dhāl assimilated into tāʾ and became a doubled dāl.
rows.anchor: وأصله مذتكر على وزن مفتعل من الذكر فأدغمت الذال في التاء ثم قلبت دالا مشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question magnifies and marvels at punishment and warnings as terrifying beyond description; singular punishment beside plural warnings signals abundant mercy and warnings before one punishment fell.
rows.anchor: استفهام تعظيم وتعجيب أي كانا على كيفية هائلة لا يحيط بها الوصف والنذر جمع نذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi identifies the closing statement about making the Quran easy as an oath-marked sentence.
rows.anchor: الخ جملة قسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated statement at the end of four narratives signals that each story alone should prompt recollection and restraint, though none was taken as a lesson.
rows.anchor: وردت في أواخر القصص الأربع تنبيها على أن كل قصة منها مستقبلة بإيجاب الأدكار كافية في الازدجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Quran easy for the Prophet’s people by revealing it in their Arabic, enriching it with admonitions, and varying threats and promises.
rows.anchor: وبالله لبد سهلنا القرآن لقومك بأن أنزلنا على لغتهم كما قال فإنما يسرناه بلسانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For remembrance” means for reminding and taking admonition.
rows.anchor: أي للتذكير والاتعاظ

rows.speaker: الحسن عن النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Hasan reports from the Prophet that without God’s statement that the Quran was made easy for remembrance, tongues could not bear to speak it.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن عن النبي عليه السلام لولا قول الله ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر لما أطاقت الألسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes and emphatically denies the existence of anyone who takes heed, phrased so strongly that nobody can answer yes.
rows.anchor: إنكار ونفي للمتعظ على أبلغ وجه وآكده حيث يدل على أنه لا يقدر أحد أن يجيب المستفهم بنعم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says he recited “mudhakkir” with dhāl, but the Prophet corrected it to “muddakir” with dāl.
rows.anchor: وعن عليه السلام بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال : قرأت على النبي عليه السلام فهل من مذكر بالذال

rows.speaker: برهان القرآن
rows.claim: Burhan al-Quran says this refrain closes the accounts of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, and Lot, whose fates warn Quran readers to heed and admonish others.
rows.anchor: قال في برهان القرآن قوله فكيف كان الخ ختم به قصة نوح وعاد وثمود ولوط لما في كل واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, Noah is the heart subdued by the commanding soul and human traits; God answers his plea, lets luminous spiritual qualities overcome animal darkness, and saves him on their ship while destroying the lower self.
rows.anchor: وفي الآيات إشارة إلى مغلوبية نوح القلب في يد النفس الأمارة بغلبات الصفات البشرية عليه حتى دعا ربه فأجابه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Flood’s heavenly waters signify compassion, mercy, and generosity from the world of spirits, while springs from human earth signify knowledge and realities.
rows.anchor: وأفاض من سماء الأرواح العلوية مياه الرأفة والرحمة والكرامة ومن أرض البشرية عيون المعارف والحقائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When unveiling and direct vision increase, spirits yearn for annihilation; God carries them in ships of protection, guided by providential care.
rows.anchor: إذا زاد الكشف والعيان تستشرف الأرواح على الفناء فيدخلها الله في سفن الصعمة ويجريها بشمال العناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets and saints are ships of divine care: those who follow their way escape error and misery and enter the Merciful’s protection.
rows.anchor: أن الأنبياء والأولياء سفن عنايته تعالى يتخلص العباد بهم من الاستغراق في بحار الضلالة وظلمات الشقاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The criminals” refers to polytheists among both earlier and later peoples.
rows.anchor: أي المشركين من الأولين والآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi explains their state as ruin and blazing fires.
rows.anchor: أي في هلاك ونيران مسعرة والتسعير آتش نيك آفروختن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is that they are astray from truth in this world and face fires in the next.
rows.anchor: وقيل في ضلال عن الحق في الدنيا ونيران في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase “on the day they are dragged” can attach to their being in ruin and fire, or to an estimated verb introducing what they are told afterward.
rows.anchor: أي كائنون في ضلال وسعر يوم يجرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar is a proper name for Hell and is therefore indeclinable; another view takes it as the fifth level of Hell, from a verb meaning to scorch and change.
rows.anchor: سقر علم لجهنم ولذلك لم يصرف وقيل اسم لطبقتها الخامسة من سقرته النار إذا بوخته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Touch is perception through the skin’s surface; “taste Saqar’s touch” means suffer its heat and pain, using cause for the resulting pain.
rows.anchor: والمس كاللمس وهو ءدراك بظاهر البشرة والمعنى قاسوا حرها وألمها فإن مسها سبب للتألم بها

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The lexicon explains “taste Saqar’s touch” as the first thing one experiences from it, like feeling the onset of fever.
rows.anchor: وفي القاموس ذوقوا مس سقر أي أول ما ينالكم منها كقولك وجد مس الحمى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that a martyr, a Quran reciter-scholar, and a wealthy donor are each exposed as acting for praise, then dragged face-first into the Fire.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أول الناس يقضي فيه يوم القيامة رجل استشهد أتى به فعرفه نعمه

rows.speaker: عطاء السلمي
rows.claim: ʿAta al-Sulami recounts Saʿdun challenging supplicants to examine their hearts; after their prayer brought no rain, Saʿdun invoked God by their private bond and rain fell immediately.
rows.anchor: خرجت يوما مع أصحابي نستسقي فلقيني سعدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account teaches sincerity and purification from concern for others; those who turn from God toward ego and worldly desire taste the fire of distance and abandonment.
rows.anchor: والكلام في تصحيح النية وتطهير القلب عن الغير والإخلاص تعالى ومن بقي في صفات نفسه وأعرض عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Everything” is accusative, governed by the verb explained by the following verb.
rows.anchor: من الأشياء وهو منصوب بفعل يفسره ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each thing is created with a definite measure set by wisdom, shaping its form and outward and inward qualities for the benefit attached to its creation; alternatively it was prewritten in the Tablet before occurring.
rows.anchor: متعين اقتضته الحكمة التي عليها يدور أمر التكوين فقدر بمعنى التقدير وهو تسوية صورته وشكله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet evokes God’s settled decision and a dried pen, counseling silence before what has been inscribed on the eternal Tablet.
rows.anchor: قضى الله أمرا وجف القلم سر بر خط لوح ازلي دار وخموش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi distinguishes qada as all creation’s collective existence in the Preserved Tablet and qadar as its actual existence in the world once conditions arise.
rows.anchor: وهو القدر المستعمل في جنب القضاء بالقضاء وجود جميع المخلوقات في اللوح المحفوظ مجتمعة والقدر وجودها في الأعيان

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says God wrote all creatures’ destinies fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth, while His Throne was upon water.
rows.anchor: كتب الله مقادير الخلائق كلها قبل أن يخلق السموات والأرض بخمسين ألف سنة وعرشه على الماء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says everything, including incapacity and cleverness, occurs by God’s decree.
rows.anchor: كل شيء بقدر الله حتى العجز والكيس

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet names four required beliefs: God’s oneness, his own true apostleship, resurrection after death, and belief in destiny’s good and evil.
rows.anchor: لا يؤمن عبد حتى يأمن بأربع يشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأني رسول الله بعثني بالحق

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: Ahl al-Sunna hold that good and evil are servants’ acts, for which they are rewarded or punished, yet occur by God’s will and decree; Bursevi says this refutes Qadariyya, Muʿtazila, and Kharijites.
rows.anchor: قال في كشف الأسرار مذهب أهل سنت آنست كه نيكى وبدى هرند فعل بنده است وبنده بدان مثاب ومعاقب است

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading says every scientific and concrete existent was created eternally at a definite measure matching its original disposition and capacity, with nothing added or lacking.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية خلقنا كل شيء أي موجود علمي وعيني في الأزل بمقدار معين مثل ما قال

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali says no possible world is more excellent than this one; otherwise its nonappearance would imply miserliness or incapacity in God.
rows.anchor: كما قال الغزالي رحمه الله ليس في الإمكان أبدع من هذا الوجود لأنه لو كان ولم يظهر لكان بخيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For anything God wills to create, His command is one word, “Be,” requiring no repetition and taking effect swiftly; alternatively it is one effortless act of creation.
rows.anchor: أو إلا فعلة واحدة وهو الإيجاد بلا معالجة ومعاناة

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The lexicon defines lamḥ as a furtive, swift glance, explaining the comparison to a blink.
rows.anchor: قال في القاموس لمح إليه كمنع اختلس النظر كألمح

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat glosses lamḥ as the flash of lightning or seeing something for a lightning-flash instant.
rows.anchor: وفي المفردات اللمح لمعان البرق ورأيته لمحة برق

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh connects this verse to the preceding threats against Meccan unbelievers and promises to believers: both are fixed in the Tablet and executed as swiftly as a blink.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ لما اشتملت الآيات السابقة على وعيد كفار أهل مكة بالإهلاك عاجلا وآجلا والوعد للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation equates the verse’s meaning with the statement that the Hour is like the blink of an eye.
rows.anchor: معنى الآية معنى قوله تعالى : وما أمر الساعة إلا كلمح البصر

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some Sufi masters say “Be” is not the letters kāf and nūn but the meaning through which things appear; the phrase veils that meaning from those who understand.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : ليس المراد بكلمة كن حرف الكاف والنون إنما المراد بها المعنى الذي به كان

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Every person bears an inward power of “Be”; some spiritual heirs can manifest it outwardly in this world, as when the Prophet summoned Abu Dharr at Tabuk and he appeared.
rows.anchor: وكل إنسان له في باطنه قوة كن وماله في ظاهره إلا المعتاد وفي الآخرة يكون حكم كن منه في الظاهر

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: The power of “Be” is uniquely associated with human beings because of their divine vicegerency; the source says angels and others were not given it.
rows.anchor: ثم لا يخفى أنه لم يعط أحد من الملائكة وغيرهم حرف كن إنما هي خاصة بالإنسان لما انطوى عليه من الخلافة

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawi verse says bread-making is not wisdom: true provision is God’s gift, and closing one mouth may open another to receive spiritual morsels.
rows.anchor: فهم نان كردن نه حكمت اى رهى زانكه حق كفت كلوا من رزقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse singles out drinkable, fresh water because drinking is its most important use.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص هذا الوصف بالذكر مع كثرة منافعه لأن الشرب أهم المقاصد المنوطة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muzn means cloud, singular muznah; another says it is specifically a white cloud whose water is sweeter.
rows.anchor: أي من السحاب واحده مزنة وقيل : هو السحاب الأبيض وماؤه أعذب

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: If seeing means knowing, the interrogative governs the verb; if it means sight or recognition, the interrogative clause is independent, which al-Raḍi prefers.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو اختيار الرضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could make the water briny and undrinkable; the contrast stresses how serious losing food is, since water is needed alongside food and its loss is less difficult.
rows.anchor: ملحا زعاقا لا يمكن شربه وحذف اللام في الشرطية الأولى للفرق بين المطعوم والمشروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to gratitude means thanking God for food and drink by affirming His oneness and obeying Him, or thanking Him for making the water sweet.
rows.anchor: فهلا تشكرون ما ذكر جميعا من المطعوم والمشروب بتوحيد منعمه وإطاعة أمره أو فلولا تشكرون على أن جعلناه عذبا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas describes a sea beneath the Throne from which God sends animal provisions through the heavens; angels place every measured raindrop, except the unmeasured Flood rain.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن تحت العرش بحرا تنزل منه أرزاق الحيوانات يوحي الله إليه فيمطر ما شاء

rows.speaker: بعض الحكماء
rows.claim: Some philosophers say the rainbow draws rainwater from the sea into clouds, which then release it onto the earth.
rows.anchor: إن المطر يأخذه قوس الله من البحر إلى السحاب ثم ينزل من السحاب إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others say this better displays divine power: salty sea water rises and then descends as fresh rain.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : هو أدخل في القدرة لأن ماء البحر مر فيصعد ملحا وينزل عذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain is especially valuable in Arabian places without wells or flowing rivers, including Jerusalem, Yanbu, and Jeddah, so God reminds people of fresh water’s blessing.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن بعض بلاد العرب ليس لها آبار ولا أنهار جارية فلا يشرب أهلها إلا من المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fresh water signifies divinely gifted knowledge and gnosis; God could turn the water of unveiling into salt flowing from veiling, ignorance, and error, so spiritual gifts also demand gratitude.
rows.anchor: وفيها إشارة إلى ماء معرفة والعلم الإلهي فإنه ليس بالكسب والاجتهاد بل بمحض عطاء الله تعالى ولو شاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A well may yield no water, salt water, or fresh water; even fresh well water is unlike pure rain, as formal scholarship differs from inspired knowledge of truth, which prophets and saints receive without error.
rows.anchor: من حفر بئرا فإما أن يصل إلى الماء أو لا فإن وصل فإما أن يكون ذلك الماء مالحا أو عذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sufi knowledge is received through remembrance and gift without arranging premises, while formal scholars use reflective reasoning; seekers must prepare their receptivity like farmers who till and sow before rain.
rows.anchor: فعلمهم تذكري ليس لهم احتياج إلى ترتيب المقدمات بخلاف علماء الرسوم فإن علمهم تفكري هتاج إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit descends with rain and appears in forms suited to each stage; at completion in the womb, God’s breathing of spirit names its manifestation, since reason cannot grasp it directly.
rows.anchor: ثم اعلم أن الروح ينزل بالمطر وله تعين في كل نشأة بما يناسبه فعند تمام الخلقة في الرحم ينفخ الله تعالى الروح

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet uncovered his head when rain began and said it had just come from its Lord.
rows.anchor: وكان عليه السلام يكشف رأسه عند نزول المطر ويقول حديث عهد بربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain teaches people to receive divine manifestations with a suitably prepared receptacle; the Prophet uncovered his head because rain descends from above and the head is the human body’s highest part.
rows.anchor: فينبغي تلقي التجليات الواردة من قبل الحق بهيئة المحل كما أن النبي عليه السلام كشف رأسه وهيأ محل نزول المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tūrūnah means kindling fire, bringing it out with a fire-drill; Arabs rubbed two sticks, calling the upper one zand and the lower one zandah.
rows.anchor: أي تقدحونها وتستخرجونها من الزناد والعرب تقدح بعودين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree from which tinder comes is the marakh and ʿafar, as discussed earlier in Surat Ya-Sin.
rows.anchor: وهي المرخ والعفار كما مر في صورة يس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tinder fire reminds people of Hell because they rely on earthly fire for livelihood and should remember the promised Fire; it is also a model of Hell.
rows.anchor: جعلنا نار الزناد تذكير النار جهنم من حيث عقلنا بها أسباب المعاش لينظروا إليها ويذكروا ما أوعدوا به

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet says the fire people kindle is one seventieth of Hellfire’s heat.
rows.anchor: ناركم هذه التي يوقدها بنو آدم جزء من سبعين جزأ من حر جهنم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the fire as proof of resurrection, since producing fire from a moist tree is an extraordinary transformation.
rows.anchor: وقيل تبصرة في أمر البعث فإنه ليس أبدع من إخراج النار من الشيء الرطب

rows.speaker: عين المعاني
rows.claim: Ayn al-Maʿani treats the fire as evidence against deniers of punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: وفي عين المعاني وهو حجة على منكري عذاب القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mataʿ means benefit and provision; producing fire is useful because making or carrying it is difficult.
rows.anchor: ومنفعه وبلغة لأن حمل النار يشق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muqwīn are people staying in barren country without water, speech, or buildings, especially travelers.
rows.anchor: للذين ينزلون القواء بالفتح وهو القفر الخالي عن الماء والكلام والعمارة وهم المسافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travelers especially need fire to drive away beasts, warm themselves, dry clothes, and cook; settled people nearby are less dependent on kindling.
rows.anchor: وتخصيصهم بذلك لأنهم أحوج إليها ليهرب منها السباع ويسطلوا من البرد ويجففوا ثيابهم ويصلحوا طعامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning worldly usefulness after the reminder of Hell signals that the afterlife benefit is more important.
rows.anchor: وتأخير هذه المنفعة للتنبيه على أن الأهم هو النفع الأخروي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb aqwā means to lodge in barren land, just as aṣḥara means to enter the desert.
rows.anchor: يقال أقوى الرجل إذا نزل في الأرض القواء كأصحر إذا دخل في الصحراء

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet asks Gabriel why he never sees Michael smile; Gabriel answers that Michael has not laughed since the Fire was created.
rows.anchor: قال النبي عليه السلام لجبريل مالي أر ميكائيل ضاحكا قط

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas transmits that the least punished person in Hell wears two sandals that make his brain boil, showing Hell exceeds worldly fire; the narrator asks God for protection.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه يرفعه أن أدنى أهل النار عذابا الذي يجعل له نعلان يغلي منهما دماغه

rows.speaker: أبو الحسين المنصور
rows.claim: The inward fire is love, kindled by the seeker’s striking in the sincere lover’s heart; its tree is eternal divine care, which Abu al-Husayn al-Mansur defines as the reality of love.
rows.anchor: وشجرتها هي العناية الإلهية السرمدية يدل هذا التأويل قول العارف أبي الحسين المنصور قدس سره

rows.speaker: أبو الحسين المنصور
rows.claim: Al-Mansur says without eternal divine care, a person would not know the Book or faith.
rows.anchor: حين سئل عن حقيقة المحبة هي العناية الإلهية السرمدية لولاها ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire guides human souls toward the path of truth, while its provision is spiritual food for lovers who abstain from food and drink for many days.
rows.anchor: نحن جعلناها تذكرة لأرباب النفوس البشرية ليهتدوا بنورها إلى سلوك طرق الحق ومتاعا للمقوين أي غذاء لأرواح المحبين

rows.speaker: سهل التستري
rows.claim: Sahl al-Tustari is said to have fasted for thirty days at a time.
rows.anchor: حكي عن سعل التستري رحمه الله أنه كان يطوي ثلاثين يوما

rows.speaker: أبو عقيل المغربي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAqil al-Maghribi is said to have eaten nothing for two years while residing in Mecca; the author also mentions many ascetic wayfarers.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عقيل المغربي قدس سره أنه ما أكل سنتين وهو مجاور بمكة وعن كثير من المرتاضين السالكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary says Idris reached the fourth heaven through extreme detachment: he left bodily life, associated with angels, spent sixteen years without sleep, food, or marriage, and rose to the sphere of the Sun.
rows.anchor: وإنما رفع إدريس عليه السلام إلى السماء الرابعة لمبالغته في التجريد والترويح حتى أن الروحانية غلبت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “on the day” is governed by an omitted “remember,” magnifying and making the day of Judgment fearful.
rows.anchor: منصوب باذكر المقدر تعظيما لليوم وتهويلا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is the Resurrection, when God revives the dead for recompense.
rows.anchor: والمراد يوم القيامة أي يحييهم الله بعد الموت للجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “All together” either emphasizes the pronoun by excluding anyone from resurrection or describes them assembled at one time.
rows.anchor: أي كلهم بحيث لا يبقى منهم أحد غير مبعوث فيكون تأكيدا للضمير أو مجتمعين في حالة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God exposes their foul deeds by stating their source or showing them as terrifying forms suited to that realm, to shame them publicly and intensify punishment; mere information would serve no purpose.
rows.anchor: من القبائح ببيان صدورها منهم أو بتصويرها في تلك النشأة بما يليق بها من الصور الهائلة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines iḥṣāʾ as exact enumeration, related to pebbles because people counted by fingers.
rows.anchor: الإحصاء التحصيل بالعدد يقال أحصيت كذا وذلك من لفظ الحصى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another gloss says iḥṣāʾ is counting with comprehensive control; it is more specific than ordinary counting, which does not entail completeness.
rows.anchor: الإحصاء عد بإحاطة وضبط إذ أصله العدد بآحاد الحصى للتقوى في الضبط فهو أخص من العد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They forgot their deeds because there were so many or because they committed them carelessly and did not believe they would matter.
rows.anchor: والحال أنهم قد نسوه لكثرته أو لتهاونهم حين ارتكبوه لعدم اعتقادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s being a witness means nothing is absent from Him; it requires recalling sins, weeping, and repenting before public exposure when excuses and pleas will not be accepted.
rows.anchor: فلا بد من استحضار الذنوب والبكاء عليها وطلب التوبة من الله الذي يحصى كل شيء ولا ينساه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is present through knowledge, not bodily presence; therefore Qur’anic language that He is present gives no basis for declaring its speaker an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن القول بأنه تعالى شهيد قول بأنه حاضر لكن بالحضور العلمي لا بالحضور الجسماني فإنه منزه عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s rhetorical question is a denial whose own negation affirms the point; it addresses the Prophet or any qualified listener and asserts certain, witnessed-like knowledge of all that is in heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: والهمزة للإنكار المقرر بالرؤية لما أن الإنكار نفي معنى ونفي النفي يقرر الإثبات فتكون الرؤية ثابتة

rows.speaker: نجم الدين الكاشفي
rows.claim: Najm al-Din al-Kashifi describes one kind of poverty as dependence on God alone, and links it to a Prophetic saying about poverty’s abasement in both abodes.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ نجم الدين الكاشفي رحمه الله : الافتقار على ثلاثة أقسام

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying describes poverty as blackening one’s face in both abodes; hadith scholars criticized “poverty is my pride,” but the author says its meaning is sound.
rows.anchor: الفقر سواد الوجه في الدارين

rows.speaker: الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Husayn defines the poor as those who remain with God, content with the course of His will in their lives.
rows.anchor: وسئل الحسين رحمه الله من الفقراء؟ قال : الذين وقفوا مع الحق راضين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some Sufis define the poor as people who abandon every attachment and look to nothing in either world but their Lord; God makes them kings and has the wealthy serve them in honor.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : هم الذين تركوا كل سبب وعلاقة ولم يلتفتوا من الكونين

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading makes the emigrants migrants from the village of the ego to the city of spirit and heart, crossing psychic and bestial wilderness through spiritual discipline.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية أبدل الله من ذوي القربى المهاجرين إلى الله

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: They leave the home of their being and the possessions of their traits and morals for their Creator, seeking His grace and the light of His pleasure and attributes.
rows.anchor: المخرجون من ديار وجوداتهم وأموال صفاتهم وأخلاقهم إلى حضرة خالقهم ورازقهم طالبين من فضله وجوده

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The spiritual migrants support God by manifesting the comprehensive divine name and support the Messenger by manifesting his outward laws; they are truthful in annihilation of self and subsistence through God.
rows.anchor: ناصرين الله بمظهريتهمالاسم الجامع ورسوله بمظهريتهم لأحكامه وشرائعه الظاهرة أولئك هم الصادقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new clause praises the Ansar, including their love for the emigrants and their complete acceptance of the emigrants receiving the spoils.
rows.anchor: كلام مستأنف مسوق لمدح الأنصار بخصال حميدة من جملتها محبتهم للمهاجرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ansar are the Aws and Khazraj, traced through their forebears to the Azd and Qahtan, whom the source identifies as the origin of the pure Arabs.
rows.anchor: والأنصار بنو الأوس والخزرج ابني حارثة بن ثعلبة بن عمرو بن عامر بن حارثة ابن امرىء القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghassan is linked to a spring near al-Juhfa where a group descended from the Azd settled and drank, taking their name from it.
rows.anchor: ومن الأنصار غسان كشداد ماء قرب الجحفة نزل عليه قوم من ولد الأزد فشربوا منه فنسبوا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of bawāʾ is parts being level or fitting together in a place, unlike nubuww, which is being ill-fitted; a place is bawāʾ when it suits its occupant.
rows.anchor: وأصل البواء مساواة الأجزاء في المكان خلاف النبو الذي هو منافاة الأجزاء يقال مكان بواء إذا لم يكن نابيا بنازله

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet chose a settled place for relieving himself as he would for his residence.
rows.anchor: وروي إنه عليه السلام كان يتبوأ لبوله كما يتبوأ لمنزله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabawwaʾū means taking a place as a home and settling there; since faith is not a physical place, several figurative parses are offered.
rows.anchor: وتبوأوا لمنزل اتخاذه منزلا والتمكن والاستقرار فيه فالمتبوأ فيه لا بد أن يكون من قبيل المنازل والأمكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possible constructions treat the state as a place, include adherence in the verb, or understand “they took the abode and embraced, accepted, or preferred faith,” with a verb omitted by ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وقيل ضمن التبوؤ معنى اللزوم وقيل تبوأوا الدار وأخلصوا الإيمان أو قبلوه أو آثروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi suggests the original sense was “the abode of faith”: Medina is faith’s home and the home of migration, while the conjunction explicitly praises their faith because residence alone is insufficient.
rows.anchor: لعل أصل الكلام والذين تبوأوا دار الإيمان فإن المدينة يقال لها دار الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Before them” means before the emigrants’ migration, with an omitted noun understood; the Ansar did not all believe before the emigrants, since some believed before the Hijra and others after.
rows.anchor: أي من قبل هجرة المهاجرين فقدر المضاف لأن الأنصار لم يؤمنوا قبل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One commentator says the Ansar in their homeland embraced Islam and built mosques two years before the Prophet’s arrival.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم مراد أنصار ندكه درديار خود ايمان آوردند وبد وسال يش ازقدوم حضرت مساجد ساختند

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad reads making faith one’s home as adhering to it and fulfilling all its rights, including public rites; the Ansar preceded the emigrants in public practice, not in inward sincerity.
rows.anchor: قال في الإرشاد : يجوز أن يجعل اتخاذ الإيمان مباءة ولزومه وإخلاصه عبارة عن إقامة كافة حقوقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward reading makes the abode the heart, home of truth and sincerity, and faith a special, God-given faith established within it.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى دار القلب التي هي دار الصدق والإخلاص وإلى الإيمان الاختصاصي الوهبي بتحقيقه وتثبيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ansar love emigrants for migrating out of love for faith, and because God and His beloved love them; the beloved’s beloved is beloved.
rows.anchor: يحبونهم من حيث مهاجرتهم إليهم لمحبتهم الإيمان ولأن الله وحبيبه أحباهم وحبيب الحبيب حبيب

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar takes the phrase as an allusion to the Ansar’s hospitality toward guests.
rows.anchor: وفي كشف الأسرار كنايتست از مهمان دوستى أنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hajah means something one needs; the phrase denies that the Ansar felt a need or desire for what the emigrants received in spoils and other gifts.
rows.anchor: وغيره ومن بيانية يقال خذ منه حاجتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negating that they found such a need in themselves is more emphatic than saying they knew of none; another reading denies their desire for the gifts, and another denies resentment or envy.
rows.anchor: والمراد من نفي الوجدان نفي العلم لأن الوجدان في النفس إدراك علمي وفيه من المبالغة ما ليس في يعلمون

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines need as dependence on something together with desire for it.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الحاجة إلى الشيء الفقر إليه مع محبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means they prefer the emigrants, with its object omitted; they put them first in all means of livelihood.
rows.anchor: أي يقدمون المهاجرين فالمفعول محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their generosity could mean a man with two wives giving one up so an emigrant could marry her.
rows.anchor: حتى أن من كان عنده امرأتان كان ينزل عن إحداهما ويزوجها واحدا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ithar means giving another something that you yourself need.
rows.anchor: والإيثار عطاؤك ما أنت تحتاج إليه

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet says every gathering has included both generous and miserly people except the Ansar, who were all generous and had no miser among them.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر لم يجتمع في الدنيا قوم قط إلا وفيهم أسخياء وبخلاء إلا في الأنصار فإن كلهم أسخياء ما فيهم من بخيل
